subject: Next steps: deployment mode & migration details for Finova
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Elena Park <elena.park@finova.com>, Aaron Li <aaron.li@finova.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 25 Feb 2026 15:12:00 -0800
Subject: Post-demo: deployment modes & migration checklist

Hi Elena / Aaron —

Great to meet you both on the call earlier. Quick recap and proposed next steps based on what we discussed:

1) Short summary of options (high-level)
- Hosted API: fastest path, no infra for Finova to manage; good for early production traffic and fast iteration.
- Dedicated: reserved GPU pools for predictable throughput and lower per-token cost at scale; keeps data logically isolated on our side.
- Private (VPC / on-prem): full control for regulated data, can be air-gapped; longer onboarding and procurement.

2) From the call, key signals you gave that matter for mode selection:
- Current latency target: p95 < 250ms for request/response (chat flows).
- Data residency / compliance: certain PII must not leave your VPC for regulated products.
- Migration origin: you mentioned a legacy on-prem GPU cluster + some traffic through a general LLM API.

3) Practical recommendation for next step:
- If you want to move quickly and validate product fit, start with Hosted for non-regulated traffic and a Dedicated pilot for core flows that need predictable SLOs.
- If you require strict data residency immediately, we should scope Private (VPC or on-prem) — that will add procurement and infra lead time (6–10 weeks typical).

4) Ask for you (please reply with):
- A single-page inventory: where inference currently runs (examples: public LLM API provider names, on-prem cluster specs, model sizes you use) — attach if possible.
- Rough monthly token estimate or QPS during peak.
- Any compliance documents/standards that mandate data stay in your VPC.

Attached: RWDW-deployment-comparison.pdf (short matrix), Finova-MAP-next-steps.xlsx (draft mutual action plan).

If that sounds right I can loop in my infra SE (Rishi) for a technical deep-dive next week.

Thanks,
Marissa

Redwood Inference

Date: Thu, 26 Feb 2026 09:07:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-demo: deployment modes & migration checklist

Marissa / Elena —

Adding a few technical notes from my side to help scope the deep dive:

- If Finova is migrating from a legacy GPU cluster (NVIDIA V100 / A100) on-prem, please include current model artifacts (PyTorch/TensorFlow checkpoints) and whether you are using 16-bit, 8-bit quantization, or custom kernels. That affects our Private onboarding and Dedicated config.
- For Dedicated: we can match A100 / H100-class throughput; we’ll propose a quantization profile that keeps quality near baseline while lowering memory.
- For Hosted: many customers use a hybrid approach (Hosted for dev + low-risk traffic, Dedicated for core mission flows). We support token-level routing policies to split traffic by route.

Also linking internal checklist that I’ll use in the deep-dive: https://redwood-internal.atlassian.net/browse/INF-3421 (internal SE playbook).

Proposed technical-deep-dive slot: Tue 03 Mar 2026 10:00–11:00 PST. Will include: Rishi (SE), Vivek (CS), Marissa (sales), Finova infra/ML lead.

-Rishi
Rishi Malhotra | Senior Solutions Engineer
rishi.malhotra@redwood.com

From: Elena Park <elena.park@finova.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Aaron Li <aaron.li@finova.com>
Date: Thu, 26 Feb 2026 11:18:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-demo: deployment modes & migration checklist

Marissa / Rishi —

Thanks for the clear recap — this is helpful. A few clarifications from our side:

- Current infra: three-node on-prem cluster running mixed GPU fleet (2x V100, 1x T4) managed by our infra team. We have ~200M tokens/month today, expect 3x growth in 6 months. We are also passing lower-sensitivity traffic to OpenLLM-based endpoints hosted in our cloud account.
- Compliance: for product "SecureAdvisor" we need to keep PII inside our VPC; other products can run from a hosted vendor.
- Cost sensitivity: finance will want to see a 12-month cost comparison (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private) including onboarding fees.

We can provide a short inventory doc — attaching a one-pager with current cluster spec and traffic numbers.

Questions:
1) If we start with Dedicated for core flows, how disruptive is a later migration to Private (VPC) if compliance requires it?
2) Do you have reference timelines and an estimated cost band for a Dedicated pilot (3-node equivalent throughput)?

Happy to take the 03 Mar deep-dive if the time holds.

Thanks,
Elena Park
Director of Machine Learning Engineering | Finova Financial
elena.park@finova.com
[Attachment: Finova_cluster_inventory_20260226.pdf (1 page)]

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Elena Park <elena.park@finova.com>, Aaron Li <aaron.li@finova.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 26 Feb 2026 11:43:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-demo: deployment modes & migration checklist

Elena —

Thanks for the inventory doc — that's exactly what we needed. Quick answers:

1) Migration path Dedicated -> Private: designed to be smooth. We persist model versions and can replicate KV cache / routing policies. Typical effort: configuration + security review + provisioning (4–8 weeks) depending on procurement. We will provide a migration playbook and a sandbox VPC to validate.
2) Dedicated pilot estimate: for a 3-node A100-equivalent pilot we typically see a $20k–$35k/month committed cost band (depends on sequence lengths, batching). I’ll run a sizing exercise after we have exact QPS/seq length and will follow up with a draft pricing carve-out in the MAP.

Next steps:
- Confirm the 03 Mar 10:00 PST deep-dive (I'll send a calendar invite).
- Elena: share the short inventory + any compliance excerpts (SaaS restrictions).
- Vivek: can you prepare a short procurement checklist and typical SOW milestones we use for Private?

Appreciate it — we’ll aim to have a pilot proposal by next Friday.

Best,
Marissa

Redwood Inference
